results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 40 aligned outline summaries state the controlling idea of their spec paragraph (p01 to p40, including the reordered p14/p13 and p18/p19/p17); the three callout entries are page format and match no spec paragraph.

Five units were marked two_ideas. Introduction ¶2 (thesis and route) and Checklist ¶1 (synthesis and checklist) are single spec units by design. Three Modes ¶1 holds the definition, the three names and the tie to the four team types, all of which p06's controlling idea names. Team API ¶4 holds the four things worth copying, the fourth of which is the user and measure, as p19 declares. Checklist ¶2 holds the callback and the hand-off, both in p40's controlling idea. None holds an idea outside its spec paragraph.

Every unit serves the supporting claim its section declares: scene and unchosen-mode units S1; mode units S2; team API, charter and AI units S3; the two patterns S4; sources-disagree S5; anti-patterns S1/S3; worked example S2 to S4. No unit is an orphan.

Every quotation is introduced with its authors or book and followed by what it shows; Team Topologies, Six Simple Rules and Scaling People are named with their concept (modes, team API, typical pairings, resisting clarification, team charter). The one-team-at-a-time limit is given as 'The authors' rule of thumb'. Extensions are marked: the fifth part ('my extension and not the source's'), the dated time box ('my recommendation'), and the queue/meeting reading and the three exits (in 'The author's synthesis'). All six tables and Figure 1 have a lead-in or caption saying what they show; scenario numbers are interpreted; AI claims carry Emerging/Speculative with 'my observation' and a confirmation condition.

Every declared transition_in is expressed at its boundary (for example 'X-as-a-Service has the opposite cost' for contrast at p09, 'A recurring meeting between teams is not always a symptom, though' at p14, 'The wall is why one of this book's sources would distrust the whole idea' at sources-disagree, 'The change had a price' at p32). The anti-patterns opener expresses the declared contrast but names its carry-over inaccurately; that is recorded under flow_is_followable.

results.finding: The lead opens on the Corvane scenario with its numbers and turns to the reader's own case; no dictionary definition, throat-clearing or announcement without a claim.

The conclusion sorts what holds by how settled it is, states a synthesis and a course of action, and does not merely restate or open a new argument; the question it leaves open is the declared hand-off.

Checklist ¶1 gives the synthesis ('one decision at two moments') and the so-what (read each recurring meeting and queue as 'which mode is this, and did anyone choose it?'), and the checklist carries the end date and the one-page team API.
Checklist ¶2 returns to the platform team of five and says what was missing: 'It lacked a page: a defined service, a way to ask and a promise.'

The intro reader predicted all ten sections in the spec's order, the thesis in both halves, the filled-in team API for Corvane's platform team and Team Topologies as the main source. The only miss is where the failure patterns are tied in (predicted in the unchosen-mode section, found in anti-patterns), which is not a roadmap promise.

The cold reader answered: collaboration nobody chose, with no end date; target X-as-a-Service, or a boundary change if no interface can be drawn; needed first: a defined interface with an owner and a consumer who can use it without talking, with the collaboration treated as past its date and due an exit. This matches the expected answer in all three parts.

The platform team's team API is filled in with concrete content in every part (what is owned and not done, how to ask by case, four promises with numbers, channels and escalation, current interactions with mode and end date) and can be copied and edited.

Each of the three patterns names its user and a measure: the team API (an engineer in a product team who has never spoken to the platform team; share of needs met without a person, and whether a consumer can state the promises), choosing a mode (the two leads and their shared manager; same mode and end date named separately, at most one collaboration, falling wait), the end date (the two leads; number of collaborations past their date).
